rated_messages.input_message: As smokers are usually with you in this location, it's really important that you're not with them when they smoke. Consider avoiding this place if possible until things settle down.
When you begin to crave a cig, concentrate on your reasons for not smoking. Keep a list on your phone and look at it when you feel yourself beginning to falter.
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
You were often stressed in this location and this might trigger urges. What can you do to reduce your stress here? If you can avoid this place until things settle down, then do.
Imagine this urge as just another backseat passenger that hopped in after seeing other people smoke. You are the driver and you still get to call the shots.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!

Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
Instead of smoking, write a quick note to yourself explaining why ditching cigs is important to you. Carry it with you and read it when you feel like lighting up.
